proof_rows.derivation_english: The named successor-addition axiom AS. No earlier proof line is used.
proof_rows.formula_english: For every \(x\) and \(y\), adding the successor of \(y\) gives the successor of their sum.

proof_rows.derivation_english: The named zero-addition axiom AZ. No earlier proof line is used.
proof_rows.formula_english: For every \(x\), adding zero leaves \(x\) unchanged.

proof_rows.derivation_english: An instantiation implication, with \(n\) substituted for \(x\). The consequent has not yet been asserted by this line.
proof_rows.formula_english: If the successor-addition axiom holds for every \(x\), it holds with \(x\) replaced by the parameter \(n\).

proof_rows.derivation_english: An instantiation implication, with \(n\) substituted for \(x\). It will be applied to the axiom at reader line 2.
proof_rows.formula_english: If zero-addition holds for every \(x\), adding zero to \(n\) leaves \(n\) unchanged.

proof_rows.derivation_english: An instantiation implication, with zero substituted for \(y\). Its universal antecedent is obtained later at reader line 7.
proof_rows.formula_english: If the successor-addition relation holds for every \(y\) with \(n\) fixed, it holds at zero.

proof_rows.derivation_english: Atomic equality-substitution implication. Its substitution hole is inside the successor, so this is a nested-term transport; it does not by itself assert the final equality.
proof_rows.formula_english: If \(n\) plus zero equals \(n\), then the displayed successor equality can be transported from the first term to the second.

proof_rows.derivation_english: Modus ponens uses reader line 1 as antecedent and line 3 as implication.
proof_rows.formula_english: With \(n\) fixed, adding the successor of any \(y\) gives the successor of their sum.

proof_rows.derivation_english: Modus ponens uses reader line 2 as antecedent and line 4 as implication.
Modus ponens uses reader line 7 as antecedent and line 5 as implication.
proof_rows.formula_english: Adding the successor of zero to \(n\) gives the successor of the sum of \(n\) and zero.

proof_rows.derivation_english: Modus ponens uses reader line 8 as antecedent and line 6 as the outer implication. One implication remains.
proof_rows.formula_english: If adding the successor of zero to \(n\) gives the successor of the sum of \(n\) and zero, it gives the successor of \(n\).

proof_rows.derivation_english: Modus ponens uses reader line 9 as antecedent and line 10 as implication.
proof_rows.formula_english: Adding the successor of zero to \(n\) gives the successor of \(n\).

proof_rows.derivation_english: Universal generalization of reader line 11. The original indexed hypothesis list is empty, so no unused free hypothesis blocks generalization.
proof_rows.formula_english: For every \(n\), adding the successor of zero gives the successor of \(n\).
